stories.headline: Gulf States Press Trump to Continue Iran War Until Islamic Regime Falls

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain asked Trump to continue attacks against Iran until the regime is crippled enough for regime change or stops being a regional threat, per AP report citing Gulf and Israeli officials
key_facts.excerpt: The Gulf States have asked US President Donald Trump to continue the attacks against Iran until the Islamic regime ceases to be a threat to the region, according to a Monday report by The Associated Press

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia and UAE are leading the push to increase military pressure on Tehran, while Oman and Qatar maintain a more neutral stance favoring diplomacy
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia and the UAE are currently leading efforts to increase military pressure on Tehran... Oman and Qatar continue with their more 'neutral' stance of supporting a diplomatic solution

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia believes any negotiated deal would be insufficient and Iran's nuclear program must be fully destroyed before talks can begin
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia believes that any deal reached with Iran would not be enough to guarantee security for the Arab countries in the region, with most estimates believing that, before any negotiation, there is a need to fully destroy Iran's nuclear program

key_facts.fact: Netanyahu said the war is 'beyond its halfway point' and proposed rerouting Gulf energy pipelines through Saudi Arabia to the Red Sea and Mediterranean, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz
key_facts.excerpt: Long-term solutions include rerouting energy pipelines westward, across Saudi Arabia to the Red Sea and Mediterranean, bypassing Iran's geographic choke point

sources.title: Gulf States pressure Trump to continue war with Iran until fall of Islamic regime

stories.headline: Iran-US Peace Talks Stall: 15-Point Plan Meets Five Iranian Counter-Demands

key_facts.fact: The US proposed a 15-point plan delivered to Iran via Pakistan, but no face-to-face meeting has been set despite Pakistan's offer to host discussions; Iran denies negotiations are taking place
key_facts.excerpt: It has been more than a week since President Donald Trump announced the U.S. was in conversation with Iran, but despite offers by Pakistan to host in-person discussions, no face-to-face meeting has been set and Iran denies negotiations are taking place

key_facts.fact: US demands include: Iran cannot enrich uranium on its soil, must surrender 10,000 kg of fissile material, and accept oversight mechanisms — all red lines for Tehran
key_facts.excerpt: Iran can't enrich uranium on its soil — a demand that has been a nonstarter for Tehran in past discussions. He also said that as part of the 15 points, Iran would have to give up its stockpile of 10,000 kilograms of fissile material

key_facts.fact: Iran countered with five demands: halt to 'aggression and assassinations,' mechanisms to prevent re-imposition of war, reparations, and recognition of Iran's sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz (which carries 20%+ of global oil)
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has countered with its own five points, including a complete halt to 'aggression and assassinations by the enemy,' the establishment of concrete mechanisms to ensure that war won't be reimposed on Iran, war damages and reparations, and international recognition of Iran's sovereign right to exercise authority over the Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Trump claimed 'great progress' on Truth Social; Iran's Foreign Affairs spokesperson called US demands 'very excessive, unrealistic and irrational' and denied any negotiations
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said Monday on Truth Social that the U.S. was in serious discussions with a 'new, and more reasonable, regime'... Baghaei on Monday also denied, yet again, that there have any direct negotiations between the U.S. and Iran

key_facts.fact: Pakistan army chief Syed Asim Munir is the key intermediary; top diplomats from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Egypt have held talks about possible talks
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan army chief Syed Asim Munir, whom Trump has referred to as his 'favorite field marshal,' has become a key go-between for the U.S. and Iran

key_facts.fact: Iran allowed 20 ships through the Strait of Hormuz plus 10 last week, but still controls the passageway; Secretary Rubio questioned who is making decisions in Iran, noting no one has seen new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei
key_facts.excerpt: Rubio said it was unclear who was even making the decisions in Iran, questioning whether Iran's new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, is really in power. 'No one has seen him. No one has heard from him'

sources.title: Are there talks to end the Iran war? Depends on which side you ask
Trump 'pretty sure' of Iran deal, but can Pakistan-led efforts end the war?

stories.headline: Powell: Fed Can 'Wait and See' as Iran War Creates Inflation-Jobs Tension

key_facts.fact: Speaking at Harvard, Powell said the Fed can wait to see how the Iran war affects the economy, noting policymakers typically look through oil price shocks
key_facts.excerpt: We feel like our policy's in a good place for us to wait and see how that turns out

key_facts.fact: Powell acknowledged tension between the Fed's two mandates: downside risk to jobs suggests keeping rates low, upside risk to inflation suggests otherwise
key_facts.excerpt: There's sort of downside risk to the labor market, which suggests keep rates low, but there's upside risk to inflation, which suggests maybe don't keep rates low. You've got tension between the two objectives

key_facts.fact: Rate hike bets have 'all but disappeared' after Powell's remarks; the Fed is now expected to hold rates this year vs. 50+ bps of cuts priced in before the war began
key_facts.excerpt: His remarks appeared to calm financial markets that last week had reflected rising expectations the Fed may try to head off higher inflation by raising rates. Those rate hike bets have all but disappeared

key_facts.fact: Inflation has run above the 2% target for about five years through a series of shocks (COVID, tariffs, and now energy); Powell said 'no one knows how big' the energy shock will be
key_facts.excerpt: inflation has been running above the central bank's 2% target for about five years, boosted by a series of shocks... We're getting now an energy shock: no one knows how big it will be

key_facts.fact: The Fed held rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% earlier this month; Powell's leadership term ends May 15, with Trump nominee Kevin Warsh set to succeed him
key_facts.excerpt: The Fed left its overnight benchmark interest rate steady in the 3.50%-3.75% range earlier this month... Powell's leadership term ends May 15

sources.title: Powell says Fed can 'wait and see' how war affects inflation

stories.headline: FDA Approves High-Dose Spinraza for Spinal Muscular Atrophy

key_facts.fact: FDA approved Biogen's high-dose (50mg) Spinraza formulation for spinal muscular atrophy, reversing a surprise rejection in September 2025 that cited manufacturing concerns
key_facts.excerpt: After a surprise rejection in September last year, the FDA has signed off on a high-dose formulation of Biogen's spinal muscular atrophy drug Spinraza

key_facts.fact: New regimen requires two 50mg loading doses 14 days apart plus 28mg maintenance every four months, replacing four 12mg induction doses — significantly faster loading
key_facts.excerpt: Instead of four induction doses with the original 12-mg formulation, the newly approved version will only require patients to receive two 50-mg loading doses 14 days apart, followed by 28-mg maintenance injections every four months

key_facts.fact: Spinraza sales peaked at $2.097B in 2019 but slumped below $1.55B in 2025 after Roche's competing oral SMA drug Evrysdi won FDA approval; high-dose approval could reinvigorate the franchise
key_facts.excerpt: Spinraza was approved in December 2016 and quickly became a top-selling product for Biogen, reaching its peak in 2019 when it earned $2.097 billion. Sales have since slowed down, slumping to below $1.55 billion in 2025

key_facts.fact: Approval was backed by Phase 2/3 DEVOTE study showing significantly better motor skill outcomes than sham control; updated data also showed improvements in event-free survival
key_facts.excerpt: Monday's approval was backed by data from the Phase 2/3 DEVOTE study, which found that the higher-dose drug led to significantly better motor skill outcomes than a sham control

sources.title: Biogen Bounces Back With FDA Nod for High-Dose Spinal Muscular Atrophy Drug

key_facts.excerpt: Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, issued an order requiring safety and privacy guardrails for artificial intelligence companies contracting with the state

key_facts.fact: The order mandates that AI companies working with California protect privacy and civil liberties, framed as a contrast to the Trump administration's push for AI in military applications
key_facts.excerpt: I just signed an executive order to actively make sure AI companies working with the state protect privacy and civil liberties. While Trump pressures companies to deploy AI for autonomous weapons

key_facts.fact: The order comes as 55% of Americans say AI will do more harm than good and 65% oppose building data centers in their community, per a new Quinnipiac poll
key_facts.excerpt: Americans are increasingly turning against artificial intelligence, with growing majorities saying they fear the fast-moving technology
